clue.text: Timepieces fine old boy looks at

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
OB is the standard abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil
to look at something is to watch it

explanation.surface: A former pupil admires some timepieces of good quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Fob watches are pocket timepieces worn on a chain, so they are a kind of timepiece.

clue.text: Misleads over 'crown', type of paper

parts.note: to mislead someone is to fool them
a cap is a crown, as on a tooth or the top of something

explanation.surface: A paper type is said to be deceptively named after a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a traditional large size of writing and printing paper, named after a jester's-cap watermark.

clue.text: Terrible noise abuser in South American capital

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A loud troublemaker is making a terrible din in a South American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Buenos Aires is the capital city of Argentina, in South America.

clue.text: Supplier of beef from Scottish city overlooking former county

parts.note: Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland
Angus was a Scottish county before the 1975 reorganisation

explanation.surface: Beef comes from a Scottish city that looks out over an old county.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'overlooking' places the city above the county.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish breed of cattle raised for its prized meat.

clue.text: Remove dirt from heels in church

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a ship heels when it leans over to one side

explanation.surface: Someone cleans muddy shoes inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heels' looks like shoes but is a verb meaning tilts.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse something is to wash it clean, taking away the dirt.

clue.text: Choose artist to highlight Agamemnon's daughter

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist is picked to put a figure from Greek legend in the spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Electra is the child of King Agamemnon and Clytemnestra who avenges her father.

clue.text: Endless industrial action in Norwegian port

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are cut away

parts.note: a go-slow is a form of industrial action where workers deliberately slow down

explanation.surface: Dock workers in a Norwegian port are staging a never-ending strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo, the capital of Norway, is also a major seaport on its fjord.

clue.text: Sink it, first of gunboats

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the next word only

parts.note: the opening letter of gunboats

explanation.surface: An order to scuttle a ship, starting with the gunboats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to droop or subside downward, the same as sinking.

clue.text: Boy in unit is punctual

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: one is a single unit
a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad in a military unit always turns up promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on time means arriving at the agreed hour, which is what punctual describes.

clue.text: Mother-to-be seems, to some extent, grossly overweight

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: found running across to-be and seems

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman looks rather heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese is the medical term for being severely overweight.

clue.text: White-flowered plant? See number round byre, spreading

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: eight is a number

indicators.note: something spreading loses its shape, so these letters are laid out anew

parts.note: a byre is a cowshed; its letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant with white blooms is pointed out growing all round a cowshed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a synonym here; it simply directs the solver to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild herb with white flowers, once used to treat eye complaints.

clue.text: Behave arrogantly? Horse did racing across uncut grass

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over it, so one piece goes either side of the other
racing letters are in a mad rush, so they end up in a fresh order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged
the rough is the long uncut grass on a golf course

explanation.surface: A horse galloped across a patch of long grass, behaving rather high-handedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride roughshod over others is an idiom for treating them arrogantly, with no regard for their feelings.

clue.text: English novelist died on Welsh mountain

parts.note: C. P. Snow was an English novelist
D is the abbreviation for died
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer from England met his death on a Welsh peak.
explanation.walkthrough: C. P. Snow wrote the Strangers and Brothers novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.

clue.text: A lot of money in study? I'm staggered

indicators.note: staggered letters stumble out of line and land in another order

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds a pile of cash in their study and is astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggered' reads as amazed, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is an informal idiom for a considerable amount of cash.

clue.text: An extremely short time in Adriatic resort before transfer

parts.note: Split is a resort city on Croatia's Adriatic coast
to second someone is to transfer them temporarily to other duties

explanation.surface: A tourist has only moments at a Croatian resort before the coach transfer leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A split second is an idiom for a tiny fraction of a second, an instant.

clue.text: Regular sea lane, rough for the most part

indicators.note: rough treatment knocks the letters about into a different order

parts.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shipping route that is usually choppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean usually or in most cases.

clue.text: Leaves with British writer on railway

parts.note: Graham Greene was a British novelist
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: An author travels by train and departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun for foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is green foliage, a collective name for plant leaves.

clue.text: Study inside B&B, say, one's main source of income

indicators.note: inside places one piece within another, here straight after the opening letter

parts.note: the ampersand is read as the word and
to read a subject is to study it
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Working from home in a guest house is how someone mainly earns a living.
explanation.walkthrough: B&B, a bed and breakfast, is split open so the study word sits after its first letter, and 'say' is the final piece rather than a hint of an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread and butter is an idiom for a person's basic livelihood, the work that pays the bills.

clue.text: New part for redevelopment in Belgian province

indicators.note: something up for redevelopment is going to be rebuilt in another form

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh district earmarked for rebuilding in part of Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is both a city and the surrounding province in Flanders, northern Belgium.

clue.text: Expert marksman's gone to sleep on watch

parts.note: a limb that has gone to sleep is numb, or dead
to eye something is to watch it

explanation.surface: A sniper has nodded off while on sentry duty.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadeye is informal for a crack shot, someone who rarely misses a target.

clue.text: Light type used by the French

parts.note: a type is a kind
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A lightweight typeface is popular with French printers.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle a fire is to light it, set it burning.

clue.text: Within view, popular location by the sound of it

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: this tells the solver to go by how the words are pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a site is a location

explanation.surface: A trendy spot can be seen from here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in sight is visible, able to be seen from where one stands.

clue.text: Sportsman permitted to enter rearranged heat

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within the other
rearranged means put into a new order

parts.note: the four letters to be rearranged
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A runner is allowed into a re-run qualifying race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heat' sounds like a race round, which suits the surface, but it is only letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person who competes in sport, especially track and field.

clue.text: Rich ornamentation on metal — mother has a tasteless display

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
taken as written
making a scene is an unseemly public display

explanation.surface: Mum puts on a vulgar show of her ornate metal jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene work is inlay of gold or silver on steel, a decorative style linked with Damascus.

clue.text: Spoil, smash up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ram something is to smash into it

explanation.surface: A command to wreck something by breaking it to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to damage or spoil its appearance or quality.

clue.text: Almost caught, English scientist and inventor

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a fish that is caught is hooked

explanation.surface: An English inventor was nearly captured.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Hooke was a 17th-century English natural philosopher who formulated the law of elasticity and built microscopes.

clue.text: Make listener nervous, at first

parts.note: the ear is the organ of listening

indicators.note: at first keeps just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of nervous

explanation.surface: Making someone who is listening feel jittery from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' looks like an instruction to cause something, but it is the definition, as in make a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to earn it, gaining income through work.

clue.text: Initially Sir Pieter, (Dutch portrait painter), to capture knight, did magnificently

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece surrounds the others
initially keeps only the opening letter of each of the next words

parts.note: the opening letters of Sir and Pieter
Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born portrait painter at the English court
N is the chess notation for a knight
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dutch painter knighted in England is said to have excelled.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed painter is Lely himself, born Pieter van der Faes; 'did' is part of the wordplay, so the definition is the adverb alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendidly means in a magnificent, impressive manner.
